mainTopic: The meal-time disputes of בית שמאי and בית הלל and the blessings of מוצאי שבת
overview: This amud explains several disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל about meals. First, the גמרא shows that their argument over washing hands or mixing the כוס first depends on whether a cup with an impure outside may be used. בית הלל add a second reason: the meal should come right after נטילת ידים. Next, they argue about where to put the drying cloth, on the table or on the cushion. The root question is whether a table that is a שני may be used, and בית הלל add that hand-washing for חולין is only rabbinic. Then the גמרא discusses sweeping versus washing after the meal, which depends on whether one may use an attendant who is an עם הארץ, and it gives the הלכה. The amud then turns to מוצאי שבת: the order of the blessings, where רבא follows רבי יהודה's version of בית הלל, and the wording of the fire blessing, which רב יוסף explains as one light versus many lights. It ends with why we do not bless on the spices of גוים, and opens a ברייתא about fire that 'rested.' The meaning of that term is explained on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the quoted law: only the outside of the vessel is impure
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה finishes. When the outside of a vessel is impure from liquids, the inside, rim and handles stay pure. If the inside becomes impure, the whole vessel is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its inside, its rim, its ear-shaped handle and its handles are pure. If its inside became impure, the whole vessel is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote of a משנה about a vessel whose outside became impure through liquids. This law is the background for the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impurity that comes from liquids is a rabbinic level of טומאה, and it only affects the part of the vessel that was touched. If only the outside was touched, the inside and the handles stay טהור. The inside is the main part of a vessel, so if the inside becomes impure, the whole vessel is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Its inside, the part of the vessel that holds the drink
The rim, the edge that sticks out around the top
Here it means the straight handles of the vessel, not a person's hands

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'יָדָיו' means the handles of the vessel. It does not mean a person's hands. Hands only enter the discussion in the next steps.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because the outside of a cup can be impure while the inside stays pure, a practical question comes up: may you drink from such a cup? That question is the real argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל.

phrases.english: its inside and its rim
and its ear-shaped handle and its handles are pure.
phrases.notes: 'Handles' means the vessel's straight handles.

phrases.english: If its inside became impure, all of it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the משנה (כלים) that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the outside of a vessel is impure from liquids, only the outside is impure. Impurity of the inside makes the whole vessel impure.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle actually divides בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to find the real reason behind the argument. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides accept the law of the משנה about impure outsides. So the גמרא wants to know which underlying assumption leads one side to wash hands first and the other to mix the cup first.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה just quoted as a springboard to ask about the root of the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The core principle that splits בית שמאי and בית הלל on the order of washing and mixing the כוס.

steps.title: בית שמאי forbid using a cup with an impure outside
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold that we may not use a cup whose outside is impure, because of a גזירה about drips. So they have no worry about wet hands touching such a cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold that it is forbidden to use a vessel whose outside became impure through liquids. This is a decree because of drips. So there is no need to make a decree out of concern that the liquid on one's hands will become impure from the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the view of בית שמאי. They forbid drinking from a cup whose outside is impure, so for them there is no risk from such a cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drops of wine could drip from the inside onto the impure outside, become impure, and then make the drink or the drinker impure. Because of this, בית שמאי forbid using the cup at all. Nobody will be holding such a cup, so there is no reason to worry that wet hands will touch it. That is why they can wash hands first.

keyTerms.meaning: Its back, meaning the outside of the vessel
Liquids, which can pass on rabbinic impurity
And there is no need to make a decree

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold
it is forbidden to use a vessel
whose outside became impure through liquids,
a decree because of drips.
phrases.notes: Drops from the inside might fall onto the impure outside.

phrases.english: And there is no reason to decree
lest the liquid on the hands become impure through the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי אָסוּר לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בִּכְלִי שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרָיו בְּמַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving בית שמאי's underlying assumption.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי forbid using a cup with an impure outside because of drips. So the risk of wet hands touching such a cup never comes up.

steps.title: בית הלל permit the cup, so they worry about wet hands
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל allow using a cup whose outside is impure, because drips are uncommon. Because the cup is in use, they must worry that wet hands will touch its impure outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל hold that it is permitted to use a vessel whose outside became impure through liquids. They say drips are not common. So there is a concern that the liquid on one's hands will become impure because of the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the view of בית הלל and finishes answering the question. Their more lenient view about the cup creates a different concern about the hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל do not make a גזירה over something rare like drips, so such a cup may be used. But if a person washes first and then picks up this cup with wet hands, the water on his hands can become impure from the cup's outside. That is why בית הלל have the cup mixed first and the hands washed afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: And there is reason to be concerned

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides worry about impurity. They differ only on whether a cup with an impure outside may be used. בית שמאי forbid it (because of drips), so they wash first. בית הלל permit it (drips are rare), so they worry about wet hands touching the cup and mix the cup first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic pattern: being lenient in one area (allowing the cup) can create a stricter concern in another area (protecting the wet hands).

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel hold
it is permitted to use a vessel
whose outside became impure through liquids,
they say: drips are not common,
and there is reason to be concerned

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא יִטָּמְאוּ מַשְׁקִין שֶׁבַּיָּדַיִם מֵחֲמַת הַכּוֹס.
phrases.english: lest the liquid on the hands become impure because of the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי מוּתָּר לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בִּכְלִי שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרָיו בְּמַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite assumption of בית הלל, which completes the answer to step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית הלל permit using a cup with an impure outside because drips are rare. So they worry about wet hands touching it and have the cup mixed before washing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The argument depends on whether a cup with an impure outside may be used. That decides which concern applies, and so which order of washing and mixing each side follows.

steps.title: בית הלל's second reason: the meal comes right after washing
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל give another reason for mixing the cup first: the meal should follow right after נטילת ידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another reason: the meal must come right after washing the hands.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל add a second reason for their order: mix the cup first, then wash, then eat right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason was about טומאה: wet hands might touch the impure outside of the cup. This second reason does not involve טומאה at all. It is about keeping no gap between washing and eating, so washing should be the very last step before the meal.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual washing of the hands before eating bread

phrases.english: Another reason:
phrases.notes: בית הלל are still speaking. This is their second reason.

phrases.english: immediately after the washing of the hands comes the meal.
phrases.notes: So you mix the cup first, then wash, then eat right away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent reason for the ruling of בית הלל explained in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The meal must follow right after washing, so the cup should be mixed before washing.

steps.title: Why did בית הלל need a second reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra reason adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of saying "another reason"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why בית הלל needed a second reason when the first one already explained their view. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first reason is good, a second one looks unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what situation the second reason covers that the first one does not.

phrases.english: What is the point of "another reason"?
phrases.notes: Why add a second reason at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the additional reason given in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the second reason add that the first reason did not?

steps.title: Even by בית שמאי's own view, בית הלל's order is better
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל tell בית שמאי: even if you are right about the impure cup, our order is still better because the meal follows washing right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what בית הלל said to בית שמאי: Even according to you, who say we may not use a vessel whose outside is impure because of a גזירה about drips, our view is still better, because the meal comes right after washing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the second reason is an argument that works even if you accept בית שמאי's own position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason depended on בית הלל's view that we may use a cup with an impure outside. בית שמאי reject that, so for them the first reason has no force. The second reason does not depend on that point at all, so it still shows that בית הלל's order is better.
steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל have two reasons for mixing the cup before washing. The first depends on their own view about the impure cup. The second, תכף לנטילת ידים סעודה, works even according to בית שמאי.

phrases.english: This is what they said to them:
Beit Hillel to Beit Shammai:
Even according to you, who say
phrases.notes: בית הלל accept בית שמאי's view just for the sake of argument.

phrases.english: it is forbidden to use a vessel whose outside is impure
because we make a decree due to drips,
phrases.notes: This was explained in step 3.

phrases.english: even so, this one is better,
phrases.notes: Our order is still better.

phrases.english: because immediately after washing the hands comes the meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמְרִי לְהוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second reason holds even if we grant בית שמאי's גזירה about drips, so it strengthens בית הלל's view on בית שמאי's own terms.

steps.title: Quoting the next part of the משנה: drying the hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next dispute, about where to put the drying cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: one dries his hands, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית שמאי say the cloth used to dry the hands goes on the table, and בית הלל say it goes on the cushion one sits on. The "and so on" points to that full dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., and so on (the rest of the quote)

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: One dries, etc.
phrases.notes: A short quote of the משנה. The full line is about where to put the drying cloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the cup and opens the next dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: after drying the hands, the cloth is placed on the table.

steps.title: A ברייתא explains בית שמאי: the cloth goes on the table, not the cushion
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the cloth should not go on the cushion, because the cushion might make the wet cloth impure, and the cloth would then make the hands impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: בית שמאי say one dries his hands with the cloth and places it on the table. If you say to put it on the cushion, there is a גזירה: perhaps the liquid in the cloth will become impure from the cushion and then make the hands impure.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the reason behind בית שמאי's ruling in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cloth is wet from drying the hands. The cushion is treated as possibly impure, and wet liquid that touches something impure becomes impure itself. Impure liquid can then make a person's hands impure, so בית שמאי keep the cloth away from the cushion.

keyTerms.meaning: Cushion one sits or leans on

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the cushion is impure because of the cloth. It works the other way: the cushion may already be impure, and it passes טומאה to the wet cloth. The cloth then passes it to the hands.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Beit Shammai say:
one dries his hands with the cloth
and places it on the table.
For if you say to put it on the cushion,
there is a decree, lest they become impure:
the liquids in the cloth, because of the cushion,
phrases.notes: The cloth is wet from drying the hands.

phrases.english: and then they in turn make the hands impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים מְקַנֵּחַ יָדָיו בַּמַּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the משנה line quoted in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Put the cloth on the table, not the cushion. Otherwise the cushion may make the wet cloth impure, and the cloth would then make the hands impure.

steps.title: Why not say the cushion makes the cloth itself impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בית שמאי need the liquids to explain the danger. Shouldn't the impure cushion make the cloth impure directly?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the cushion make the cloth impure directly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just gave for בית שמאי. If the cushion is impure, why not just say it makes the cloth impure?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the cushion makes the liquids in the cloth impure, and the liquids then make the hands impure. The question is: why go through the liquids at all? The cloth itself is touching the cushion.

keyTerms.meaning: A cushion or pillow that a person sits or leans on
A cloth or towel, here used to dry the hands

phrases.english: Let the cushion make the cloth impure!
phrases.notes: Meaning: directly, without needing the liquids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the path of טומאה described in Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the cushion makes the cloth's liquids impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the cushion can pass on טומאה, it should make the cloth impure directly, so the mention of liquids looks unneeded.

steps.title: A vessel does not make another vessel impure
steps.stepSummary: The answer: one כלי cannot make another כלי impure, so only the liquids in the cloth can become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: A vessel does not make a vessel impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a fixed rule of טומאה. A כלי (the cushion) cannot make another כלי (the cloth) impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cushion's level of טומאה is too weak to pass to another כלי. Liquids are different, because the רבנן made them pick up טומאה more easily. So the danger only works through the wet liquids in the cloth.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel does not make another vessel impure
A vessel or utensil; cloth items and cushions count as כלים

phrases.english: A vessel does not make a vessel impure.
phrases.notes: The cushion and the cloth are both כלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies a general rule of טומאה that blocks the direct path
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The impure cushion could make the cloth impure directly.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כלי cannot make another כלי impure, so only the liquids in the cloth are at risk.

steps.title: Why not say the cushion makes the person impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the cushion is impure, shouldn't it make the person sitting on it impure directly?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the cushion make the man himself impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another direct path. The person is sitting on the cushion, so why worry about the cloth making his hands impure?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי's worry was that the cloth would make the hands impure. But if the cushion can make the person impure on its own, the cloth adds nothing. So their reason would make no sense.

phrases.english: Let the cushion make the man himself impure!
phrases.notes: The man is sitting or leaning on the cushion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge of the same kind as Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's concern that the cloth will make the hands impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the cushion makes the person impure anyway, it doesn't matter where the cloth is placed.

steps.title: A vessel does not make a person impure
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a כלי cannot make a person impure, so the person's hands only become impure through the wet cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: A vessel does not make a person impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with another fixed rule. A כלי like the cushion cannot make a person impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person is safe from the cushion itself. The only danger is the impure liquids in the cloth. By rabbinic rule, impure liquids can make hands impure. That is why בית שמאי say: keep the cloth off the cushion.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel does not make a person impure

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: don't put the cloth on the cushion. The cushion can't make the cloth or the person impure directly, but it can make the cloth's liquids impure, and those liquids can make the hands impure.

phrases.english: A vessel does not make a person impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12 and closes the explanation of בית שמאי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies a general rule of טומאה that blocks the direct path
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cushion makes the person impure directly, so the cloth's placement doesn't matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כלי cannot make a person impure, so the only danger is the liquids in the cloth reaching the hands.

steps.title: בית הלל: put the cloth on the cushion, not the table
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives בית הלל's view: the cloth goes on the cushion. On the table, the cloth's liquids could become impure and then make the food impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: on the cushion. Because if you say on the table, there is a גזירה: maybe the liquids in the cloth will become impure from the table, and then they will make the food impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains the other side. בית הלל worry about the table, not the cushion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל use the same kind of chain as בית שמאי, just with a different danger. The table might be impure and make the cloth's liquids impure. Those liquids would then make the food on the table impure. For בית הלל, protecting the food matters more than protecting the hands.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic protective decree: we act strictly because of what might happen
Liquids; here, the water soaked into the cloth

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree on how טומאה travels through the liquids. They only disagree about which danger to avoid: בית שמאי protect the hands (keep it off the cushion), and בית הלל protect the food (keep it off the table).

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: on the cushion.
phrases.notes: Place the drying cloth on the cushion.

phrases.english: For if you say on the table,
there is a decree lest they become impure:
the liquids in the cloth, because of the table,
and they will in turn make the food impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בית שמאי's reasoning to בית הלל's reasoning in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cloth goes on the cushion, so the table can't make its liquids impure, which would then make the food impure.

steps.title: Why not say the table makes the food impure directly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the table is impure, it should make the food on it impure anyway. Why worry about the cloth?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the table make the food on it impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בית הלל the same way it challenged בית שמאי. If the table is impure, the food is already in danger without the cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food is sitting right on the table. If the table could pass טומאה to the food directly, moving the cloth would protect nothing. So בית הלל's reason would seem pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: That is on it (literally, within it)

phrases.english: Let the table make the food on it impure!
phrases.notes: Meaning: directly, without the cloth's liquids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the path of טומאה in Step 14, the same way Steps 10 and 12 challenged בית שמאי
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's concern that the cloth's liquids will make the food impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the table makes the food impure directly, the cloth's placement adds no new danger.

steps.title: The table is only a שני, which needs liquids to pass on טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the table is a שני לטומאה. In חולין, a שני can only create a שלישי through liquids, so the table cannot make the food impure by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a table that is a שני, and a שני does not make a שלישי in חולין except through liquids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying how impure the table is. It is only a שני, a weak level of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ordinary food (חולין), a שני cannot make food into a שלישי directly. Liquids are the exception: by rabbinic rule, liquids that touch a שני become a ראשון. Those liquids can then make the food impure. So the cloth's liquids are exactly what makes the table dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy food (not תרומה or קדשים)

steps.whatToRemember: In every case here, the impure object (cushion or table) is too weak to pass טומאה directly. Only the wet liquids in the cloth can carry it. בית שמאי worry about the hands, and בית הלל worry about the food.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea in the laws of טומאה: liquids are treated more strictly and pick up טומאה more easily. That is why so many rules about נטילת ידים and meals focus on liquids.

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with a table that is a second-level impurity,
and a second-level does not make a third-level
in ordinary food, except through liquids.
phrases.notes: Liquids that touch a שני become a ראשון by rabbinic rule, so they can make food impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 and closes the explanation of בית הלל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case (the table is a שני) and applies the rule that a שני needs liquids to pass on טומאה in חולין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The table makes the food impure directly, so the cloth's placement doesn't matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The table is only a שני and cannot make חולין impure directly, so the cloth's liquids are the real danger to the food.

steps.title: What is the real root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies underneath the dispute about where to put the cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they really arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what deeper idea divides בית שמאי and בית הלל. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we saw each side's practical reasoning about the cloth and the impure table. Now the גמרא wants the one basic principle that explains why they reach opposite results.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: A standard question looking for the root principle of a dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining why בית הלל worry about the table, the גמרא looks for the root principle behind the whole dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that separates בית שמאי from בית הלל.

steps.title: בית שמאי forbid using a second-degree impure table
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold that one may not eat from a table that is a שני לטומאה, because of a גזירה to protect כהנים who eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold that it is forbidden to use a table that is a שני. This is a decree because of those who eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first half of the answer. בית שמאי say you may not use a table that is a שני לטומאה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שני cannot make חולין impure without liquids, but it can make תרומה impure. בית שמאי worried that a כהן might eat תרומה on such a table, so the חכמים forbade using it even for חולין. So in their view the table is always pure, and putting the cloth on it causes no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree of the חכמים

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold:
It is forbidden to use a table that is a 'second' (in impurity),
a decree because of those who eat terumah.
phrases.notes: A שני makes תרומה impure, so a כהן could become confused.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי אָסוּר לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּשֻׁלְחָן שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 by giving בית שמאי's side of the root principle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי forbid using a table that is a שני because of a גזירה about תרומה, so in their view the table is pure and the cloth may go on it.

steps.title: בית הלל allow using a second-degree impure table
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל hold that one may use a table that is a שני, because כהנים who eat תרומה are careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל hold that it is allowed to use a table that is a שני, because those who eat תרומה are careful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of the answer. בית הלל allow using a table that is a שני, so such tables may be in use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל see no need for a decree, because כהנים are careful and will check a table before eating תרומה on it. Since a table may really be a שני, a wet cloth placed on it could become impure and make the food impure. That is why בית הלל say to put the cloth on the cushion.
steps.whatToRemember: The dispute comes down to one question: may you use a table that is a שני? בית שמאי say no, so the table is pure and the cloth can go on it. בית הלל say yes, so the table might be impure and the cloth goes on the cushion.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel hold:
It is permitted to use a table that is a 'second,'
those who eat terumah are careful.
phrases.notes: So there is no need for a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי מוּתָּר לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּשֻׁלְחָן שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by giving בית הלל's opposing side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית הלל permit using a table that is a שני because כהנים are careful. So the table may be impure, and the cloth should go on the cushion.

steps.title: בית הלל's second reason: hand-washing for חולין is not from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds another reason for בית הלל: washing hands for חולין is not a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another reason: washing hands for חולין is not from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second reason that the ברייתא gives for בית הלל. It begins with the words דבר אחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new kind of reason. It does not talk about the table. It compares how serious impure hands are with how serious impure food is. Washing hands for ordinary food is only a rabbinic rule.

phrases.english: Another reason:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נְטִילַת יָדַיִם לְחוּלִּין מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: There is no washing of hands for non-sacred food by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר אֵין נְטִילַת יָדַיִם לְחוּלִּין מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא to quote an extra reason given for בית הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing hands for חולין is only מדרבנן, not a Torah law.

steps.title: Why does בית הלל need a second reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra reason adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of saying 'another reason'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why בית הלל add this second reason when the first one seemed enough. This sets up the explanation in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason explained why the table is a worry. It is not clear what job the second reason does. The גמרא wants to know what gap it fills.

phrases.english: What is 'another reason' (coming to add)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the second reason quoted in step 20 is for.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What gap in בית הלל's argument the second reason fills.

steps.title: The expected challenge: why protect food but not hands?
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל expect בית שמאי to ask: why worry that the food will become impure, but not worry that the hands will become impure from the cloth on the cushion?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what בית הלל said to בית שמאי: If you will say, why is food different that we worry about it, and why are hands different that we do not worry about them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the second reason answers a challenge that בית הלל expect from בית שמאי. This step states the challenge, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the cloth on the cushion protects the food. But the cushion may be impure, which could make the liquids in the cloth impure, and those liquids could then make the hands impure (see steps 9-13). So בית הלל seem to protect food while ignoring the same danger to hands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (an expected objection)

phrases.english: This is what they said to them:
Beit Hillel to Beit Shammai:
And if you will say, what is different
regarding food, that we are concerned,
and what is different regarding hands,
that we are not concerned?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמְרִי לְהוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי וְכִי תֵּימְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 21 by stating the challenge that the second reason will solve.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's ruling to put the cloth on the cushion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems inconsistent to protect food from the table while exposing hands to the cushion.

steps.title: Better that hands become impure than food
steps.stepSummary: Since washing hands for חולין is only מדרבנן, it is better to risk the hands than the food, whose impurity has a Torah basis.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, this is better, because washing hands for חולין is not from the Torah. It is better that the hands become impure, since their impurity has no Torah basis, and that the food not become impure, since its impurity has a Torah basis.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל answer the challenge with the second reason. If one of them must be at risk, it is better to risk the hands than the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The impurity of hands for חולין is only a rabbinic rule. Food impurity has a root in the Torah. So when we cannot protect both, we protect the food, which is the more serious matter.
steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's second reason weighs the two risks. Hands for חולין are only a rabbinic matter, but food impurity has a Torah root. So the cloth goes on the cushion to protect the food, even if the hands might suffer.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean washing hands is optional. It is a binding rabbinic law. The point is only that when we must choose, the Torah-level concern for food comes first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general approach in הלכה: when two concerns clash, the one with a Torah basis gets priority over a purely rabbinic one.

phrases.english: Even so, this is preferable,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין נְטִילַת יָדַיִם לְחוּלִּין מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: since there is no washing of hands for non-sacred food by Torah law.
It is better that hands become impure,
which have no basis in Torah law,
and that food not become impure,
which has a basis in Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 and explains what the דבר אחר of step 20 adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ranking of severity: a rabbinic concern gives way to a concern with a Torah basis.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hands and food should be protected equally, so בית הלל seem inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Food has a Torah basis and hands for חולין do not, so protecting the food comes first.

steps.title: Quoting the next dispute in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the next dispute in the משנה, about sweeping versus washing hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: one sweeps the house, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next line of the משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup line that opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about the table, the cushion, and hand impurity. Now the גמרא moves to a new dispute: after the meal, which comes first, sweeping the eating area or washing מים אחרונים. The full explanation comes in the ברייתא that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: They sweep or clean the area
"And so on." The rest of the quote is understood.
House. Here it means the area where they ate.

steps.confusionAlert: Here מְכַבְּדִין means "sweeping" or "cleaning," not "honoring." It comes from the same root as כבוד, but in this context it is about cleaning the floor.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: one sweeps, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote of the opening words of the next part of the משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the table and cushion and moves to the next dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי hold that sweeping the eating area comes before washing hands.

steps.title: בית שמאי: sweep first so the food is not ruined
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that בית שמאי require sweeping before washing, because washing first would ruin the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: בית שמאי say that one sweeps the house and washes hands afterward. If you say that one washes hands first, you end up ruining the food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives בית שמאי's reason. Washing first would waste food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that leftover food is still on the floor or table. Washing hands before cleaning up would ruin it. So בית שמאי say: first clear the area, then wash.

keyTerms.meaning: "The רבנן taught." This introduces a ברייתא.
Washing hands. Here it means מים אחרונים after the meal.

steps.whyThisMatters: The issue behind this dispute is the prohibition of wasting or ruining food, which comes back in רבי יוחנן's ruling at the end.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Beit Shammai say
one sweeps the house (the eating area)
and afterward washes the hands,
for if you say
that one washes the hands first,
you end up ruining the food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sweep first, then wash, so the food is not ruined.

steps.title: Why does washing first ruin the food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that בית שמאי reject washing first, and asks what exactly the reason is.
steps.simpleTranslation: But בית שמאי do not hold that washing hands comes first. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask exactly how washing first would ruin food. This sets up the short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said food would be ruined, but it did not say how. The גמרא wants to identify the exact problem behind בית שמאי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not hold this view

phrases.english: But washing of the hands, according to Beit Shammai,
first, they do not hold this.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact mechanism behind the reason given in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exact concern makes washing first ruin the food?

steps.title: Because of the crumbs
steps.stepSummary: The reason is the leftover crumbs, which the washing water could splash on and spoil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the crumbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the food at risk is the leftover crumbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water from washing hands could splash onto crumbs left on the floor and spoil them. Ruining food is not allowed, so the crumbs must be cleared away first.

phrases.english: Because of the crumbs.
phrases.notes: The washing water would splash on the crumbs and spoil them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מאי טעמא question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The concern is crumbs being spoiled by the washing water.

steps.title: בית הלל: a learned attendant leaves only tiny crumbs
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that a learned attendant picks up crumbs the size of a כזית, so only crumbs smaller than a כזית are left.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: if the attendant is a תלמיד חכם, he picks up the crumbs that are a כזית and leaves the crumbs that are smaller than a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל explain why washing first is not a problem. The important crumbs have already been removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל agree that food must not be ruined. They say a learned attendant first removes every crumb as big as a כזית. The small crumbs that remain do not count as important food, so splashing water on them is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar, who knows the הלכה
The size of an olive, a standard halachic measure

steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל do not say ruining food is permitted. They say the crumbs that matter (a כזית) are removed, and only tiny crumbs remain.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
if the attendant is a Torah scholar,
he removes crumbs that are an olive-bulk,
and leaves crumbs that are not an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית הלל's view in the ברייתא, which answers בית שמאי's crumb concern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing may come first, because only crumbs smaller than a כזית remain, and ruining them is not a problem.

steps.title: This supports רבי יוחנן on small crumbs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that בית הלל's view supports רבי יוחנן, who rules that crumbs smaller than a כזית may be destroyed by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יוחנן, for רבי יוחנן said: crumbs that are smaller than a כזית may be destroyed by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that this ברייתא backs up a ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל allow small crumbs to be ruined by the washing water. This shows that crumbs smaller than a כזית do not fall under the prohibition of wasting food. That is exactly what רבי יוחנן ruled, even when the destruction is done directly by hand.

keyTerms.meaning: To destroy them directly by hand

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: sweep first, so the crumbs are not spoiled. בית הלל: wash first, because the learned attendant removed the crumbs of a כזית, and smaller crumbs may be ruined. This supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical rule: wasting food applies to pieces of a כזית or more. Smaller crumbs may be thrown out or destroyed.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yoḥanan.
For Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
crumbs that are not an olive-bulk
may be destroyed by hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses בית הלל's view as support for an אמורא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that crumbs smaller than a כזית may be destroyed by hand
steps.raayaSupportSource: בית הלל in the ברייתא, who allow small crumbs to be left and spoiled by the washing water

steps.title: What is the real root of the argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies underneath the sweeping-versus-washing debate.
steps.simpleTranslation: On what point do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what deeper principle causes בית שמאי and בית הלל to argue about sweeping and washing. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know each side's practical position and practical reason. Now the גמרא wants the single underlying principle that produces the two different results.

keyTerms.meaning: On what do they disagree? This asks for the root principle of a debate.

phrases.english: On what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the practical reasons to the underlying principle behind them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The core principle that separates בית שמאי from בית הלל on sweeping and washing.

steps.title: The argument depends on using an uneducated attendant
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל forbid using an attendant who is an עם הארץ. בית שמאי permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל hold that it is forbidden to use an attendant who is an עם הארץ. בית שמאי hold that it is permitted to use an attendant who is an עם הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the debate depends on whether you may use a waiter who is an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל require a learned attendant, and he always removes crumbs the size of a כזית. So only tiny crumbs remain, and washing first ruins nothing important. בית שמאי allow an uneducated attendant, who may leave real food on the table, so they require sweeping first.

keyTerms.meaning: An uneducated person who is not careful about הלכה
They hold, or they are of the opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a small practical difference about table order comes from a broader rule about who may serve at a meal.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel hold
it is forbidden to use an attendant who is an am ha'aretz.
And Beit Shammai hold
it is permitted to use an attendant who is an am ha'aretz.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי אָסוּר לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּשַׁמָּשׁ עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument depends on whether one may use an attendant who is an עם הארץ. בית הלל forbid it, and בית שמאי permit it.

steps.title: The הלכה follows בית הלל except in this case
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that throughout the פרק the הלכה follows בית הלל, except here, where it follows בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said in the name of רב הונא: In our whole chapter, the הלכה follows בית הלל, except for this case, where the הלכה follows בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical ruling. It follows בית הלל everywhere in this פרק except the sweeping-versus-washing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the הלכה follows בית הלל. This step names one exception: here we follow בית שמאי, so we sweep first and only then wash.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling follows a certain opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume this is a general rule that בית שמאי are followed. It is a single exception to the usual rule of following בית הלל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said that Rav Huna said:
In our entire chapter, the halakha follows Beit Hillel,
except for this case, where the halakha follows Beit Shammai,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the debate, the גמרא gives the practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows בית הלל throughout the פרק, except for sweeping and washing, where it follows בית שמאי.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא reverses the opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא teaches the two opinions the other way around, so the הלכה follows בית הלל here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אושעיא taught it the opposite way, so in this case too the הלכה follows בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the text. In it, the positions are switched, so there is no exception, and בית הלל are followed even here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אושעיא's version, the practice of sweeping first is attributed to בית הלל. Both versions end with the same practice, sweeping before washing. The difference is only whose name it carries, and in this version the rule of following בית הלל has no exception.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches it reversed. The two opinions are switched.

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, we sweep first and then wash. The two versions disagree only about whether this is בית שמאי's view or בית הלל's view.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Oshaya teaches it the opposite way,
and in this case too, the halakha follows Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternate reading that removes the exception named in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With the opinions reversed, the הלכה follows בית הלל even in this case.

steps.title: Quoting the next part of the משנה: candle and food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה, about the order of ברכות on מוצאי שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: candle and food, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes the next clause of the משנה so it can start discussing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This clause deals with a meal that runs into מוצאי שבת. You need to say four blessings: the candle, ברכת המזון, the spices, and הבדלה. The משנה records the order each school uses.

keyTerms.meaning: Candle. This means the blessing over light.
And so on. It shows that only the start of the quote is given.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נֵר וּמָזוֹן וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: Candle and food, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי's order is candle, then ברכת המזון, then spices, then הבדלה.

steps.title: רבא blesses on spices first
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה visits רבא and sees him say the blessing on spices before the candle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה happened to come to רבא's house. He saw רבא say the blessing over spices first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a challenge. רבא does something that seems to go against the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the משנה, both schools say the candle blessing first. רבא said the spices blessing first, so the next step will question his practice.

keyTerms.meaning: He happened to come, or he visited

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא.
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda happened to come to Rava's house.
He saw Rava
reciting a blessing over spices first.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that sets up a challenge based on the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's practice was to say the spices blessing before the candle blessing.

steps.title: Both schools put the candle first
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה challenges רבא: both בית שמאי and בית הלל say the candle blessing first, so why did you start with spices?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree about the blessing on light. As it is taught, בית שמאי say: candle, food, spices, הבדלה. And בית הלל say: candle, spices, food, הבדלה. So why did you start with spices?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר יהודה challenges רבא. Both schools agree that the candle comes first, so starting with spices goes against everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about where ברכת המזון and the spices go. Both, however, put the candle in first place. רבא's practice seems to follow neither opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since. It introduces a point everyone accepts.
The blessing that separates שבת from the weekday

phrases.english: He said to him: Now, since

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל אַמָּאוֹר לָא פְּלִיגִי,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel do not disagree about the light,
as it is taught: Beit Shammai say:
Candle and food, spices and havdala.
And Beit Hillel say:
Candle and spices, food and havdala!
phrases.notes: Implied: so why did you bless on spices first?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִכְּדִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל אַמָּאוֹר לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the story of step 35 into a direct challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's practice of saying the spices blessing before the candle blessing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both schools put the candle first, so starting with spices goes against both opinions.

steps.title: רבא explains why he blessed on spices first
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the version of the משנה where both sides put the candle first follows רבי מאיר. According to רבי יהודה, בית הלל say spices come first, and then the candle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא answered after him: That is the opinion of רבי מאיר. But רבי יהודה says that בית שמאי and בית הלל did not disagree about ברכת המזון, which comes first, or about הבדלה, which comes last. What did they disagree about? About the light and the spices. בית שמאי say light, then spices. בית הלל say spices, then light.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends what he did. The version of the משנה that his questioner quoted is only רבי מאיר's version, and there is another version from רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר יהודה assumed the משנה's order is the only version, and in it both sides say the candle blessing first. רבא brings a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה reports the מחלוקת differently. In רבי יהודה's version, the only argument is light versus spices, and בית הלל put spices first. So רבא was simply following בית הלל as רבי יהודה reports them.

keyTerms.meaning: Food; here it means בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן
The blessing that separates שבת from the weekday
Light; the blessing over the candle or fire
Spices; the blessing over sweet-smelling spices

steps.confusionAlert: The two תנאים, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, are not arguing about the הלכה here. They disagree about how to report what בית שמאי and בית הלל said. Each one transmits the מחלוקת differently.

phrases.english: Rava answered after him:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: The version of the משנה in which both sides put the candle first

phrases.english: but Rabbi Yehuda says

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about Grace after Meals, that it comes first
and about havdala, that it comes last.
About what did they disagree?
About the light and about the spices:
for Beit Shammai say
over the light, and afterward the spices,
and Beit Hillel say
the spices, and afterward the light.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָנֵי רָבָא בָּתְרֵיהּ: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate tannaitic version of the dispute (רבי יהודה versus רבי מאיר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל require the candle blessing before spices, so רבא acted against everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהודה, בית הלל put spices before the candle, and רבא followed that version.

steps.title: The people follow בית הלל as reported by רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the common practice follows בית הלל according to רבי יהודה's version: spices first, then the candle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The people were accustomed to act like בית הלל, according to רבי יהודה's version.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא's practice with a report from רבי יוחנן about what people actually do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles which version is followed in practice. People follow בית הלל as reported by רבי יהודה, not as reported by רבי מאיר. So in this case, the blessing on spices is said before the blessing on the candle.

keyTerms.meaning: According to (the view or version of)

steps.whatToRemember: In this case, the practice follows בית הלל as reported by רבי יהודה: spices first, then the candle. This supports what רבא did.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The people were accustomed to act like Beit Hillel
according to Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer with the established practice
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Practice follows בית הלל according to רבי יהודה: spices before the candle.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's dispute about the fire blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה, where בית שמאי say the fire blessing uses the word שֶׁבָּרָא.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: 'Who created...' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is moving to a new topic. It quotes the next part of the משנה to set up רבא's explanation, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית שמאי say the blessing is 'שֶׁבָּרָא מְאוֹר הָאֵשׁ' (Who created the light of fire). בית הלל say 'בּוֹרֵא מְאוֹרֵי הָאֵשׁ' (Who creates the lights of fire). The 'כּוּ׳' tells us the quote continues in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the quote continues in the source

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: 'Who created,' etc.
phrases.notes: Full משנה: ב״ש say 'שברא מאור האש'; ב״ה say 'בורא מאורי האש'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the order of blessings to the wording of the fire blessing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה records a dispute over the wording of the fire blessing.

steps.title: רבא explains that the dispute is about the meaning of בּוֹרֵא
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that everyone agrees בָּרָא means 'created' in the past. The argument is whether בּוֹרֵא also means past, or only future.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: About בָּרָא, everyone agrees it means 'created.' Where they disagree is about בּוֹרֵא. בית שמאי hold that בּוֹרֵא means 'will create in the future.' בית הלל hold that בּוֹרֵא also means 'created.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains what בית שמאי and בית הלל are really arguing about in the fire blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the blessing must praise הקב״ה for fire He already created. So nobody objects to בָּרָא, since it clearly means past. בית שמאי reject בּוֹרֵא because they read it as future: 'He will create.' בית הלל say בּוֹרֵא can also mean past, so it works fine.

keyTerms.meaning: That He will create in the future

steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל are not saying בָּרָא is wrong. Everyone agrees בָּרָא is fine. The only question is whether בּוֹרֵא can also mean past.
steps.whyThisMatters: Our הבדלה text follows בית הלל: 'בּוֹרֵא מְאוֹרֵי הָאֵשׁ.' רבא's explanation, however, is challenged in step 41 and replaced by רב יוסף's explanation in step 42.

phrases.english: Rava said:
About 'bara,' everyone agrees
that it means 'created' (in the past).
Where they disagree is about 'boreh':
Beit Shammai hold
'boreh' means that He will create in the future,
and Beit Hillel hold
'boreh' also means 'created' (in the past).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּ״בָרָא״ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה clause quoted in step 39
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees בָּרָא is valid. The dispute is whether בּוֹרֵא can mean past (בית הלל) or only future (בית שמאי).

steps.title: רב יוסף challenges רבא with three פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף attacks רבא's claim that בּוֹרֵא might mean only the future, by quoting three פסוקים where בּוֹרֵא clearly describes past creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: It says 'Who forms light and creates (בּוֹרֵא) darkness,' 'Who forms mountains and creates (בּוֹרֵא) wind,' and 'Who creates (בּוֹרֵא) the heavens and stretches them out.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רבא's explanation from step 40. He brings three פסוקים where the word בּוֹרֵא is used for things הקב״ה already created.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said בית שמאי might hold that בּוֹרֵא means only 'will create.' But darkness, wind, and the heavens were all created long ago, and the פסוקים still say בּוֹרֵא. So בּוֹרֵא clearly can mean past creation, and it is hard to say anyone disagrees about that.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a source

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
"Who forms light and creates darkness"
phrases.notes: ישעיה מ״ה:ז — darkness was created in the past

phrases.english: "Who forms mountains and creates wind"
phrases.notes: עמוס ד׳:י״ג

phrases.english: "Who creates the heavens and stretches them out"
phrases.notes: ישעיה מ״ב:ה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's explanation of the argument in step 40.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the argument is whether בּוֹרֵא can mean the past
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פסוקים use בּוֹרֵא for things already created, so בּוֹרֵא clearly includes the past and no one could deny it.

steps.title: The real argument is one light or many lights
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a new explanation: everyone agrees both words mean 'created.' The argument is whether to say מאור (light) or מאורי (lights), based on whether fire has one light or many.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: About בָּרָא and בּוֹרֵא, everyone agrees that both mean 'created.' They argue about מאור (light) versus מאורי (lights). בית שמאי hold there is one light in fire, and בית הלל hold there are many lights in fire.
steps.whatsHappening: Since his challenge knocked out רבא's explanation, רב יוסף offers a new one. The argument is not about the verb at all. It is about whether to say 'light' (singular) or 'lights' (plural).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that רבא's approach is being replaced. Both verbs are fine according to everyone. בית שמאי say 'שברא מאור האש' because fire has one light. בית הלל say 'בורא מאורי האש' because a flame has several colors of light (red, white, green).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why our נוסח of הבדלה follows בית הלל: 'בורא מאורי האש,' with the plural 'lights.'

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
phrases.notes: אלא signals that the previous explanation is dropped

phrases.english: Regarding bara and boreh,
everyone agrees
that they mean 'created';
where they disagree is about 'light' versus 'lights.'
For Beit Shammai hold
there is one light in fire,
and Beit Hillel hold
there are many lights in fire.
phrases.notes: A flame has several colors

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's explanation after the challenge in step 41.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the point of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about the verb בָּרָא versus בּוֹרֵא (past versus future).
steps.terutzMaskana: The verbs are agreed upon. The argument is the noun: one light (מאור) or many lights (מאורי).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that both בָּרָא and בּוֹרֵא mean 'created.' The dispute is מאור (one light in fire, בית שמאי) versus מאורי (many lights, בית הלל).

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the many-lights explanation
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records בית הלל telling בית שמאי that there are many lights in fire, which supports רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: בית הלל said to בית שמאי, 'There are many lights in fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב יוסף's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows בית הלל arguing about the number of lights in the fire, not about the verb. That fits רב יוסף exactly and confirms that the argument is מאור versus מאורי.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: Final explanation: everyone agrees about בָּרָא and בּוֹרֵא. בית שמאי say מאור (one light). בית הלל say מאורי (many lights), and we follow בית הלל.

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
There are many lights in the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's explanation from step 42.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that the argument is about one light versus many lights
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting בית הלל: הרבה מאורות יש באור

steps.title: Why not bless over the spices of gentiles?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule against blessing over the candle and spices of גוים. The candle is understood, but why are the spices forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'We do not bless over the candle or the spices of גוים.' The candle makes sense, because its fire did not rest on שבת. But the spices, what is the reason we do not bless on them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next clause of the משנה. It accepts the reason for the candle but asks why spices of גוים should be a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A candle lit by a גוי burned during שבת, so it is a light that 'did not rest,' and we only bless in הבדלה over light that rested. Spices have no such connection to שבת. So the גמרא needs a different reason for the spices.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not make a ברכה
It makes sense regarding (the first case), but...

phrases.english: "We do not bless..." etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: not on the candle or spices of גוים

phrases.english: Granted, the candle, because it did not rest;
but spices, what is the reason not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason we may not bless over the spices of גוים

steps.title: רב: the case is a party of גוים for עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the משנה is talking about a party of גוים, and such parties are usually for עבודה זרה, so the spices are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Here we are dealing with a party of גוים, because a party of גוים is usually for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question: the spices are forbidden because they come from a party of גוים, which is assumed to be connected to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We may not get any benefit from things used for עבודה זרה, and certainly may not bless on them. Since a gathering of גוים is assumed to serve עבודה זרה, its spices fall under that problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A party or gathering of non-Jews

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Here we are dealing with a party of gentiles,
because an ordinary party of gentiles
is for idolatry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The spices come from a party of גוים, which is assumed to be for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The משנה lists עבודה זרה separately later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: the end of the משנה separately forbids the candle and spices of עבודה זרה, which implies the first clause is not about עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the end of the משנה teaches, 'We do not bless over the candle or the spices of עבודה זרה,' that implies the first part is not dealing with עבודה זרה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's answer by pointing to the end of the same משנה. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first clause, about גוים, were already about עבודה זרה, the משנה would not need a separate clause for עבודה זרה. The extra clause suggests the first one has a different reason, so רב's explanation seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it teaches

steps.confusionAlert: This is a challenge, not a conclusion. Step 47 answers it.

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
"We do not bless over the candle

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עַל הַבְּשָׂמִים שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: nor over the spices of idolatry,"
it follows that the first clause
is not dealing with idolatry!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's answer in step 45.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the first clause is about a party for עבודה זרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא names עבודה זרה separately, so the רישא must be about something else. Otherwise the סיפא would be repeating the רישא.

steps.title: The end of the משנה gives the reason for the first part
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא מסורא answers the challenge to רב. The משנה is written as 'what is the reason' style: the second clause about עבודה זרה explains why the first clause forbids the candle and spices of גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא from סורא said: The משנה is speaking in a 'what is the reason' style. It means: What is the reason we do not bless over the candle and spices of גוים? Because a party of גוים is usually for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 46, which asked why the משנה lists עבודה זרה separately if the first clause was already about עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the משנה had two separate rules, so the first rule could not be about עבודה זרה. רבי חנינא says it is really one rule plus its reason: the second clause explains the first. That saves רב's explanation completely.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is saying: what is the reason' — the second part of the text explains the first part
רבי חנינא from the town of סורא
Usually / by default, when nothing else is known
A party or feast of non-Jews

steps.whatToRemember: The candle and spices of a party of גוים are not used for הבדלה, because such parties are assumed to be for עבודה זרה. The end of the משנה is the reason, not a separate rule.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה as two separate lists. According to רבי חנינא, the עבודה זרה clause is the 'why' behind the גוים clause.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina of Sura said:
The Mishnah is speaking in a 'what is the reason' style:
phrases.notes: The second clause explains the first clause.

phrases.english: What is the reason we do not recite a blessing

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַנֵּר וְלֹא עַל הַבְּשָׂמִים שֶׁל גּוֹיִם —
phrases.english: over the candle or over the spices of non-Jews?
Because an ordinary party of non-Jews
is for idol worship.
phrases.notes: And the candle and spices of idol worship may not be used for a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 46 and defends רב's explanation from step 45.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the structure of the משנה: the second clause is the reason for the first, not a separate rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lists two separate rules, so the first rule (גוים) must not involve עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is one rule with its reason: the candle and spices of גוים are forbidden because their parties are usually for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: A blessing is said over fire that rested, not over fire that did not rest
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches a new rule for הבדלה: one blesses over fire that 'rested' (שבת), but not over fire that 'did not rest.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Fire that rested — we bless over it. Fire that did not rest — we do not bless over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about which fire may be used for the הבדלה blessing. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a rule but uses an unclear word, 'rested.' It does not say what it means for fire to 'rest.' That gap is what the גמרא will ask about next.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Fire that rested — we recite a blessing over it,
and fire that did not rest — we do not recite a blessing over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the idea of a light that 'did not rest' (mentioned in step 44 about the candle of גוים) and brings a ברייתא that states the rule in general.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In הבדלה, the blessing is said over fire that 'rested,' not over fire that 'did not rest.'

steps.title: What does 'rested' and 'did not rest' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the ברייתא's terms 'rested' and 'did not rest.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'rested,' and what is 'did not rest'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the words in the ברייתא. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fire cannot literally rest, so the word must mean something specific. The גמרא wants to know which fire counts as 'rested' and which does not, so the rule can actually be used.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? — asks for a definition

phrases.english: What is meant by 'rested,' and what is meant by 'did not rest'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the key terms in the ברייתא from step 48.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of fire that 'rested' (שבת) versus fire that 'did not rest' (לא שבת).
